issues.t: Automatic transmission slips or fails
issues.sym: Late or harsh shifts, the engine revving between gears, a flashing overdrive (O/D) light, slipping, or the truck refusing to move in drive or reverse.
issues.why: The four- and five-speed automatics in these years wear internally, and transmission failure is the most-reported problem on the 2002 Mountaineer. Owners commonly report rebuilds between 70,000 and 140,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell. If it slips or the O/D light flashes, have the codes read right away and avoid towing or hard driving until it is diagnosed.

issues.t: Transmission slips, surges or won't shift
issues.sym: The engine surges or the truck jerks when pulling away or climbing hills, shifts are delayed or harsh, or it gets stuck in one gear.
issues.why: Internal wear in the five-speed (V6) and six-speed (V8) automatics, sometimes helped early on by a computer reprogram but often ending in a rebuild.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes and fluid checked and ask the dealer about any software updates. If it keeps slipping, get a transmission specialist to diagnose it before more damage is done.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle on the 4.0L V6
issues.sym: A rattle or buzzing from the engine for a few seconds after a cold start, or a constant rattle at idle. A check engine light for a misfire or cam timing code may follow.
issues.why: The 4.0L SOHC V6 uses three timing chains with plastic guides and tensioners that wear out. The rear chain sits at the back of the engine, so the repair is very labor-heavy.
issues.next: Do not ignore the rattle. Have a shop confirm which chain is noisy. If a chain or guide breaks, the engine can be badly damaged.

issues.t: Radiator leaks at the plastic tank seams
issues.sym: Coolant drips under the front of the truck, a sweet smell, the low-coolant level keeps dropping, or the temperature gauge climbs.
issues.why: The radiator's plastic end tanks separate from the core at the seams. Many owners have replaced more than one radiator.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant and watch the temperature gauge. Get the leak confirmed with a pressure test and replace the radiator before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Cracked thermostat housing
issues.sym: Coolant seeping or dripping near the top front of the engine, low coolant, or the engine running hot.
issues.why: The plastic thermostat housing can crack with age and heat cycles.
issues.next: Check the coolant level often and have the housing inspected for wetness or white crust. Replace the housing and thermostat together.

issues.t: Wheel bearing or hub failure
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that gets louder with speed or when turning, play in the wheel, or an ABS light.
issues.why: The wheel hubs and bearings are the most-reported repair on the Mountaineer in TrueDelta's survey, front and rear.
issues.next: Have a shop check for play and noise at each wheel. Replace a worn hub soon, as a failing bearing can overheat or let the wheel wobble.

issues.t: Worn ball joints
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, loose or wandering steering, or uneven tire wear on the front tires.
issues.why: The front ball joints wear on these heavy SUVs and are among the most common repairs reported by owners.
issues.next: Have the front end checked for play. A badly worn ball joint can separate and cause loss of control, so do not delay.

issues.t: Clunking from worn sway bar links and bushings
issues.sym: A rattle or clunk from the front over small bumps or rough roads.
issues.why: The stabilizer (sway) bar end links and bushings wear and loosen.
issues.next: Have the links checked. They are a low-cost fix, but replace them before they break.

issues.t: Cracked liftgate panel below the rear window
issues.sym: A crack in the painted panel on the liftgate below the rear glass, sometimes growing the full height of the panel, and water getting inside.
issues.why: The liftgate's plastic outer panel cracks with age and heat. Body shops say it is very common on this generation.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer whether any coverage applies. Otherwise, a body shop can replace the panel; seal the crack meanwhile to keep water out.

issues.t: Shifter breaks and won't move out of gear
issues.sym: The column gear shifter snaps or goes limp when shifting, leaving the truck stuck in Park, Drive or Reverse.
issues.why: Parts inside the steering column that link the shifter to the transmission break. Dealers have replaced the whole column.
issues.next: Do not drive if you cannot shift into Park. Have it towed and ask a shop whether a used column or a repair kit will fix it.

issues.t: Door ajar light stays on and dome lights flicker
issues.sym: The door-ajar warning stays on or chimes with doors closed, interior lights flicker or won't turn off, locks cycle on their own, or the alarm goes off.
issues.why: A worn door-ajar switch inside one of the door latches sends false signals. It can drain the battery overnight.
issues.next: Have a shop find which door reports open; the fix is usually a door latch or switch on that door.

issues.t: Plastic intake manifold cracks and leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant on top of the engine or dripping at the front, low coolant, overheating, or a sweet smell.
issues.why: The 4.6L V8's all-plastic intake manifold has a coolant passage at the front that cracks, a well-known problem with this engine.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and top up coolant. Replace the manifold with Ford's revised design with an aluminum coolant crossover.

issues.t: Spark plug blows out of the cylinder head
issues.sym: A sudden loud popping or ticking, a misfire and check engine light, and the coil on that cylinder may be damaged.
issues.why: The 2-valve 4.6L V8 has only a few threads holding each spark plug in the aluminum head, and a plug can strip them and shoot out.
issues.next: Shut the engine off and have it towed. A shop can usually repair the threads with an insert without removing the head.

issues.t: Spark plugs break during removal
issues.sym: No symptoms while driving. The problem shows up at a tune-up when the shop warns that a plug broke off in the head, raising the bill.
issues.why: The 3-valve 4.6L V8 uses a two-piece spark plug that can seize in the head and snap when removed.
issues.next: Ask for a shop that uses the Ford removal procedure or a special extractor tool. Change the plugs on time; leaving them in longer makes them more likely to seize.

issues.t: Exhaust manifold leak ticking
issues.sym: A ticking noise from the engine that is loudest when cold and fades as it warms up.
issues.why: The exhaust manifold or its studs and gasket leak on the 4.6L V8.
issues.next: Have the manifold area checked for black soot marks. Fix it soon so exhaust fumes don't reach the cabin.

issues.t: Rear differential leaks or fails
issues.sym: Gear oil drips at the rear axle or wheels, a whine or howl from the rear, or clunking.
issues.why: Axle seals and pinion bearings in the rear differential wear and leak. If the oil runs low, the gears can fail.
issues.next: Check the rear axle oil level and fix seal leaks early. Have a whine diagnosed before it turns into a full differential rebuild.

issues.t: Heat stuck on hot or clicking behind the dash
issues.sym: The temperature won't change, heat blows when you want A/C, or you hear clicking behind the dash.
issues.why: The blend door or its small electric actuator breaks, so the system can't mix hot and cold air.
issues.next: Have the actuator tested. It is often reachable behind the dash or glovebox.

issues.t: Blower fan stuck on high
issues.sym: The fan runs at full speed no matter what setting you choose, or keeps running after the truck is off.
issues.why: The blower motor control module (speed controller) fails.
issues.next: Have the blower module replaced; it is usually behind the glovebox.

issues.t: A/C stops blowing cold
issues.sym: Warm or barely cool air from the vents, or the A/C compressor won't engage.
issues.why: Slow refrigerant leaks and worn or seized compressors are common as these trucks age.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested before recharging. A seized compressor usually needs a new drier and a system flush too.

issues.t: Misfire from a failed ignition coil
issues.sym: Check engine light (sometimes flashing), rough idle, shaking or loss of power, especially when climbing hills.
issues.why: Ignition coils fail with age and heat, often along with worn spark plugs.
issues.next: Have the misfire code read. A flashing check engine light means stop driving hard to protect the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Squeal from the belt tensioner or idler pulley
issues.sym: A squeal, chirp or grinding noise from the front of the engine, often worse at startup.
issues.why: The serpentine belt tensioner and idler pulley bearings wear out.
issues.next: Have the pulleys spun by hand to find the bad one. If it seizes, the belt can come off and you lose charging and steering assist.

issues.t: Alternator stops charging
issues.sym: Battery light on, dimming lights, a dead battery, or the truck dies while driving.
issues.why: The alternator wears out, and it is one of the more common repairs in TrueDelta's survey.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested before replacing the battery.

issues.t: Power window drops into the door
issues.sym: A window stops working, moves slowly, or falls down into the door.
issues.why: The window regulator cable or motor fails, or the master switch on the driver's door wears out.
issues.next: Tape the glass up if needed and have the regulator and motor checked.

issues.t: Cruise control switch can start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. In rare cases, smoke or fire near the brake master cylinder, even with the engine off.
issues.why: The speed control deactivation switch can leak brake fluid internally and overheat (recalls 07V-336 and 09V-399).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Firestone tire tread can separate (recall)
issues.sym: Vibration, a thumping noise, or a sudden tire blowout at highway speed.
issues.why: Certain Firestone tires on these trucks could lose their tread (recall 00T-005). Most were replaced long ago, but check any old spare.
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Throttle may stick or not return to idle (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stays at higher speed when you lift off the gas or after cruise control turns off, so the truck takes longer to stop.
issues.why: Problems with the speed control cable, throttle return and accelerator pedal were covered by several recalls (97V-074, 99V-062, 03V-280 and 00V-422).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Front brake line can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A soft brake pedal, brake warning light, or longer stopping distances.
issues.why: A front brake line could be damaged and lose pressure to the front wheels (recall 99V-123).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Hood can fly up if not latched (recall)
issues.sym: The hood lifts or flutters while driving.
issues.why: The secondary hood latch might not hold the hood if the main latch is not engaged (recall 99V-164).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Windshield wipers can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers stop or don't respond to the switch.
issues.why: An electronic module fault could leave the wipers inoperative (recall 00V-072).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Fuel line can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell or fuel drips under the truck.
issues.why: Fuel lines could leak and risk a fire (recall 98V-060).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Sway bar link can separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front and less stable handling.
issues.why: A sway bar fault could affect handling (recall 00V-402).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Liftgate glass bracket can break the glass (recall)
issues.sym: The liftgate glass won't stay up or it cracks or shatters when opened.
issues.why: Brackets that hold the glass support cylinders can rotate and break the glass (Ford campaign 01I-010).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Transmission cooler line bolt can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Transmission fluid drips, a burning smell, or smoke from under the truck.
issues.why: A cooler line bolt might not be tight enough, letting fluid leak onto the hot exhaust (recall 07V-453).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.

issues.t: Front seatback recliner may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: No warning in normal driving; the seatback may move backward in a crash.
issues.why: The manual front seat recliners might not hold the seatback in a rear crash (recall 10V-161).
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA recall lookup or call a Ford or Lincoln dealer. If the repair was never done, it is free under the recall.
